name: truenorth
display_name: IBM TrueNorth (28 nm, Merolla 2014): 4096 cores of 256 x 256 on a 64 x 64 mesh

named: 1-bit weights for the axon-type weight law
faithfulness.note: TrueNorth weighs a binary synapse by one of four per-neuron axon-type weights; the registered geometry declares 1-bit weights (scout_chip.md section 5.2), so a weight-quantized program on the bundle is not TrueNorth's weight law. A signed 1-bit grid has no nonzero level (q_max 0), so both doors refuse weight quantization on the bundle by name (weight_bits' applied schema, key amendment K1), and a float deployment applies no weight grid, while its payload sizes, pricing and record read weight_bits=1 (a 1-bit cell, which pricing a float run states as a boundary owned by G3), which its label names ('weight grid not applied', key amendment K2). The floorplan is the profile's 4096 cores on a 64 x 64 mesh, one core per tile (truenorth.json validity).

notes: allow_coalescing and allow_neuron_splitting are false: merolla2014a describes the core as "a self-contained neural network with 256 input lines (axons) and 256 outputs (neurons)" (the registered geometry's provenance), so a neuron integrates its own core's 256 axons only, with no inter-core partial sum (coalescing) and no core split across cores that share its inputs (neuron splitting). A deployment that needs either declares it through target_overrides with a note, and its faithfulness names it.
